solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sharply critical fraud article written for money

indicators.note: one thing written in place of another means a letter is swapped out for new letters

blocks.note: a scam is a fraud
an article is a thing, an object
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A sharp critic attacks a fraudulent piece written purely for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: SCATHING is SCAM with its M swapped for THING. 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece or a grammatical 'a', but here it is just an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathing criticism is severe and withering, a direct synonym for sharply critical.

clue.text: Lots of fish caught in southern headland unfenced

indicators.note: with its fence taken away, the word loses the letters that enclose it at each end

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a mull is a Scottish headland, as in the Mull of Kintyre

explanation.surface: A shoal of fish is netted off an open southern headland.
explanation.walkthrough: MULL loses its outer letters to leave UL, giving SCUL. Scul is an old variant of school or shoal, a group of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A scul is a shoal, an old word for a large group of fish swimming together.

clue.text: Heroin seen around Brazilian port is for me?

definitions.text: Heroin seen around Brazilian port is for me?

indicators.note: something seen around another thing surrounds it, so one word encloses the next

blocks.note: caca is a slang word for heroin
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A drug user muses that heroin found around a Brazilian port suits them.
explanation.walkthrough: Caca is a little-known slang word for heroin. Read as a whole, the clue is spoken by someone from Rio, for whom the port is home: hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carioca is a native of Rio de Janeiro, so the speaker of the clue would claim Rio as theirs.

clue.text: Tonsils removed by a game lady

indicators.note: removed suggests letters shifted out of their places and set down in a different order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sporting woman has had her tonsils taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed' reads as surgery on the tonsils, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Amygdalae is the anatomical term for the tonsils, from the Greek for almonds, after their shape.

clue.text: Rainy habitually on vacation, recently from the south

indicators.note: a word on vacation has emptied out, so only its two outermost letters stay
in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upward, from the bottom

blocks.note: the first and last letters of habitually
late can mean recently, as in 'of late'

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers complain that it has lately been habitually wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyetal is a technical term relating to rainfall, from the Greek word for rain.

clue.text: In short, no marks for citrous item gone off — it's yellow

indicators.note: cut short, the little word loses its final letter
no marks says the currency abbreviation is taken out of what follows
fruit gone off has turned bad, so the letters go wrong and fall into a new order

blocks.note: in without its last letter
taken as written
item with the M for marks taken away

explanation.surface: A citrus fruit gone mouldy turns yellow and scores nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: M stands for marks, the old German currency, removed from item. The surface makes 'yellow' describe the fruit; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Icteritious means jaundiced, of the yellow colour seen in jaundice (icterus).

clue.text: Barbarian understood to be associated with heroin

blocks.note: to have got something is to have understood it
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A savage is understood to be tied up with drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goths were a Germanic tribe who invaded Rome, so goth has come to mean a barbarian.

clue.text: Macintosh regularly getting his oats!

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every second letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A Scotsman called Macintosh is regularly getting his oats, with a nod to the slang for sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Aits is Scots for oats, which suits the Scottish name; 'getting his oats' is British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Aits is the Scots dialect form of oats, the cereal grain.

clue.text: Foreign official accepted the bill for one

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for accepted, as written on a bill of exchange
a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
e.g., for example, for one

explanation.surface: A foreign dignitary agreed to pay the bill, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: An atabeg was a Turkic ruler or high official, so a foreign official to an English reader.

clue.text: Witness canopy over bed with no end of cover

indicators.note: with no says the following letter is dropped from the word before
'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'cover'

blocks.note: a tester is a canopy above a four-poster bed
the last letter of cover

explanation.surface: Someone sees a canopy over a bed missing the bottom of its cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Teste is Latin for 'by the witness of', used in legal documents to name a witness.

clue.text: Tip shares above all in quick dialogue

indicators.note: in a down clue, one part placed above all the rest comes first in the light

blocks.note: snips are small pieces cut off, portions or shares
a nap is a racing tipster's top tip

explanation.surface: A trading tip for shares is passed on in a quick exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the second part sits above the first. 'Tip' and 'shares' look like stock-market advice, but nap is horse-racing jargon for a tipster's best bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Snip-snap is quick, sharp repartee, from the sound of scissors closing.

clue.text: Theatrical group associated with Journey's End

indicators.note: a word's end is its final letter, so only that last letter is used

blocks.note: a camp is a group sharing a viewpoint, as in 'the opposing camp'
the last letter of journey

explanation.surface: A theatre company is linked with the war play Journey's End.
explanation.walkthrough: Journey's End is a well-known First World War play by R C Sherriff, which makes the surface feel theatrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Campy describes exaggerated, showy behaviour, so theatrical in manner.

clue.text: Irish zealot on TV out to embrace the case for Eire

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters before it are rearranged
to embrace something is to hold it inside, so one set of letters wraps the other
a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
the first and last letters of Eire

explanation.surface: A fervent Irish campaigner appears on television, making the case for Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'on TV' wrap the outside letters of Eire.
explanation.definitionFit: A voteen is an Irish term for a devout or fanatically religious person, a zealot.

clue.text: Virginia gets very urgent incomplete hormone

indicators.note: incomplete means the word lacks its final letter

blocks.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
so means very, as in 'so good'
pressing means urgent

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia urgently needs a hormone treatment she cannot quite complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasopressin is a pituitary hormone that regulates water retention and blood pressure.

clue.text: Yours truly's so long with an injury in parts of foot

blocks.note: yours truly is the speaker, me
ta-ta is an informal goodbye
RSI is repetitive strain injury

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye with an injury to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly's' is read as 'yours truly is', giving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The metatarsi are the five long bones of the foot between ankle and toes.

clue.text: Tie up dispute without using technology

indicators.note: doing without something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: to litigate is to dispute in court
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A legal dispute is wrapped up without any recourse to technology.
explanation.definitionFit: To ligate is to tie or bind, especially to tie off a blood vessel in surgery.

clue.text: News sources including fringe elements in Europe

indicators.note: one word including others holds them inside it
the fringe of a word is its edge, so only its outermost letters are taken

blocks.note: springs are sources of water
the first and last letters of Europe

explanation.surface: News sources pick up fringe political movements in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News sources' reads as one phrase, but news is the definition and sources is wordplay. Speerings is Scots for enquiries, hence news or information.
explanation.definitionFit: Speering is Scots for asking or inquiring, and speerings are information gathered that way.

clue.text: Heartlessly pronounces sort of law

definitions.note: the answer completes the phrase Sod's law

indicators.note: with its heart removed, a word loses its central letters

blocks.note: to sound a word is to pronounce it

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted judge pronounces a particular kind of law.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUNDS loses its middle UN. Sod's law is the British name for the principle that whatever can go wrong will.
explanation.definitionFit: Sod's law is the British equivalent of Murphy's law, so this word fills the blank in that phrase.

clue.text: Congress included in artful caption

indicators.note: something included in another is placed within it

blocks.note: subtle can mean cunning or artful
it is slang for sex, and congress is a formal word for sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: A legislature is described in a cleverly worded caption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the US legislature but means sexual intercourse, which crosswords often reduce to IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtitle is a caption, such as the translated text along the bottom of a film.

clue.text: Double energy used to cut very large West African trees

indicators.note: letters cutting into a word split it open and sit inside it

blocks.note: OS is outsize, very large
two words for energy: pep, and E, its physics symbol

explanation.surface: A double dose of energy is needed to fell enormous African trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The opepe is a West African tree with yellowish timber.

clue.text: Showing pretty duff reform legacy in plan? Not entirely

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are made into a new arrangement
not entirely means the last word is used without its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
plan without its final letter

explanation.surface: A bad overhaul of a bequest in a plan is on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duff' looks like an adjective meaning useless, but it is British slang for the backside, so 'pretty duff' is a shapely bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Callipygean means having beautifully shaped buttocks, from the Greek for beautiful and rump.

clue.text: Laura's excited with hubbie's finish most of the time (7, three words)

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and settle in a different order
a word's finish is its final letter

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
the last letter of hubbie

explanation.surface: Laura gets excited when her husband finishes, most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy surface is a decoy; the husband supplies only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase as a rule means usually, so in most cases or most of the time.

clue.text: More than one railing at absurd Les being uncouth

indicators.note: uncouth behaviour is rough and disorderly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Several people rail at a ridiculous man called Les for his rudeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railing' looks like a verb, ranting at Les, but the definition is the noun: a fence of balusters.
explanation.definitionFit: A balustrade is a railing supported by a row of balusters, so the plural means several railings.

clue.text: Scar formation for anyone to see indeed in Casualty

indicators.note: in says one letter is placed inside the following word

blocks.note: a U-certificate film is suitable for anyone to see
a casualty is a loss, as in losses in battle
I is an obsolete spelling of aye, yes indeed

explanation.surface: Scarring is plain to see in a hospital emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: Casualty is the British term for a hospital's emergency department, and also a long-running TV drama, both decoys.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulosis is a medical term for the healing of a wound into a scar, from the Greek for scar.

clue.text: Tense game after Australia declare

indicators.note: after places the earlier parts behind the following one in the light

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for Australia, as in A$ for the Australian dollar
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a test is a Test match, an international cricket game

explanation.surface: A tense cricket Test against Australia ends with a declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declare' suggests a cricket declaration, but it is the definition in its everyday sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare or affirm something to be true.

clue.text: Note outside exhibition room for plant bodies

indicators.note: a word placed outside another goes around it

blocks.note: ti is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale
an exhibition hall

explanation.surface: A notice outside a gallery points to a display of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A thallus is a plant body not divided into stem, leaf and root, as in algae and lichens.

clue.text: Husband has power to protect one getting a lot of wives

indicators.note: a protector surrounds what it guards, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
arm can mean power or might, as in the long arm of the law
a means one

explanation.surface: A powerful husband shields one of the many wives in his household.
explanation.definitionFit: Haram is a variant of harem, the wives of a polygamous man, so a lot of wives.

clue.text: Local strike force on criminal charge

blocks.note: F is the physics symbol for force
a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

explanation.surface: Local workers walk out to force a criminal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local strike' looks like an industrial dispute; it means a dialect word for hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Frap is a dialect word meaning to strike or beat, so local in the crossword sense of regional.

clue.text: Religious VIP heads off with obscure stuff

indicators.note: with heads off, each word loses its first letter

blocks.note: dim means obscure, faint
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A religious dignitary cuts off the heads of people with strange material.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is a Muslim prayer leader, a religious figure of standing.

clue.text: First person to enter names for flight

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it

blocks.note: stars are big names, celebrities
I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: Celebrities let the first person through for a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel, but it means a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of steps between floors, a staircase.

clue.text: Short spell in holiday places?

indicators.note: short says the word is cut back by losing its final letter

blocks.note: a spasm is a short spell or fit of activity

explanation.surface: A brief stay at some holiday resorts.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a looser definition: spas are resorts, places one may holiday in.
explanation.definitionFit: Spas are resorts with mineral springs where people go to rest and take the waters.

clue.text: Muscular spasms stir awfully deep thoughts

indicators.note: done awfully means badly done, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
muses are deep thoughts, as a noun from muse, to ponder

explanation.surface: Cramps cause deep thoughts to become badly stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: Trismus is lockjaw, a spasm of the jaw muscles; trismuses is its plural.

clue.text: Look on endless bad atmosphere for mythical monsters

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: la is an old exclamation meaning look, like lo
miasm, a variant of miasma, an unhealthy atmosphere

explanation.surface: Someone looks on at an unending foul atmosphere to find legendary beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamias are female monsters of classical legend, half serpent and half woman, who preyed on children.

clue.text: Abbreviations recalled by some nostalgists?

indicators.note: some of a word means only part of it, so the letters lie within it
recalled suggests calling back, so the letters run back from right to left

blocks.note: letters inside the word

explanation.surface: Nostalgic people recall the abbreviations of their youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' fits nostalgists so well that it reads as memory, not as a signal to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigla are letters or signs standing for words, such as abbreviations in manuscripts.

clue.text: Throwing up is not wanted by relatives

indicators.note: something not wanted is thrown out, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: emesis is the medical word for vomiting
taken as written

explanation.surface: Relatives make it clear that vomiting guests are unwelcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Eme is a Scots and old word for an uncle, so emes are relatives.

clue.text: Fellow found sites for insects

indicators.note: to found metal is to melt and recast it, so the letters are moulded into a new shape

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man has discovered places where insects live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as the past tense of find, but it is the verb meaning to cast metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mantises are predatory insects, such as the praying mantis.
